history.summary: Ruins of a famous Ahom-era Vaishnavite satra on the banks of the Dehing (Burhi Dihing) river under Larua mouza, Dibrugarh district. It was patronised by Ahom kings Rajeswar Singha, Lakshmi (Lakhi) Singha and Gaurinath Singha, especially during the Moamoria rebellion (1769-1806). The satra lies largely in ruins today but retains an aura among locals who still come to worship, and it doubles as a picnic spot. IDENTITY CAVEAT: many travel sites conflate this site with the separate, living Dehing Namti Satra on the Disang river near Naharkatiya (main branch at Namti, Nazira); the ruins described here are the Dehing Satra of Dibrugarh. Coordinates are approximate to Dibrugarh town, exact siting unverified.

name: Dehing Satra
town_description: Dibrugarh is the largest city in Upper Assam, set on the south bank of the Brahmaputra amid tea gardens. Often called the tea capital of India, it hosts Dibrugarh University and is a gateway to Dehing Patkai National Park, Namdang and other Ahom-era sites.

travel.road: Reachable by road from Dibrugarh town; the ruins lie on the banks of the Dehing river
